subject: English
passage: In 2018 marine biologist Dr. Awo Badu and her research team examined the evolution of bioluminescence, the ability to produce light, which is found in some fish species but was traditionally considered an energy-costly trait with unclear benefits. Analyzing 412 deep-sea fish species, the team discovered that bioluminescence has evolved independently in multiple fish lineages on separate occasions and, importantly, has been retained once it appeared in specific lineages. Additionally, the team observed that bioluminescent species tend to have enhanced visual systems and more complex predator-prey interactions in their deep-sea environments. Therefore, the team hypothesized that bioluminescence likely ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: was once present in many shallow-water species but has since disappeared from those lineages.
choices.B: will develop in a greater number of fish species because it may serve a crucial function in deep-sea navigation.
choices.C: has been maintained in certain fish species because it provides advantages in their survival and feeding.
choices.D: created more complex visual systems in fish in the past than it does currently.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because it most logically completes the text's discussion of Badu and colleagues' investigation of the evolution and biological role of bioluminescence. The text indicates that the team found several instances of bioluminescence emerging and being retained in the lineages of various fish species the team examined. Furthermore, the text states that bioluminescent species tend to have enhanced visual systems and more complex predator-prey interactions—characteristics that would support survival advantages in deep-sea environments. Taken together, these details strongly support the hypothesis that bioluminescence has persisted in some species because it has a function that contributes to effective survival and feeding strategies in those species.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect because the text doesn't make predictions about the evolutionary future of the species Badu and colleagues examined, and although the implication of the text is that bioluminescence likely does serve a function in deep-sea environments, nothing in the text indicates that bioluminescence will become more widespread in the future.
